title: How Adam Robinson bootstrapped three SaaS companies to $1M ARR, faster each time
summary: Adam walks through Robly (17 months), Retention.com (27 weeks) and RB2B (16 weeks), all without outside funding. The thread: find an acquisition channel with no competition, and eventually build an audience first, since cold email no longer works.

principles.text: Acquiring customers is expensive because of competition; an uncontested channel with a good offer is cheap.
principles.quote: what makes acquiring customers expensive is competition. And if you have a channel that you don't have any competition in and you have a good offer, it's going to be incredibly inexpensive for you to acquire those customers.

principles.text: A channel can carry a weak product only briefly; once the list is used up, a non-competitive product stalls.
principles.quote: our product wasn't actually competitive outside of that channel

principles.text: Cold email and BDR-style outbound no longer work; pick a go-to-market that is future-proofed against it.
principles.quote: There is no way that we could have done what we did with get emails in the way that we did it today. It would be impossible.

principles.text: Make the product free and lead with founder content so the offer spreads on its own instead of paying for sales people.
principles.quote: It's this hundred million dollar value proposition that just punches you in the face. That's literally free.

principles.text: Vulnerable, honest posts about your own failures beat polished generic content on LinkedIn.
principles.quote: I'm talking about my own problems now and my own failures to revenue leaders like me in SaaS, which is very different angle.

principles.text: Treat the job as edutainment and use thought leadership ads to amplify posts that already won organically.
principles.quote: my job is edutainment. My job is to make entertaining, educational and highly compelling content about how I am building my SaaS and about how you can do it too.
